newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian navy mounts rescue for Albanian boat.
newsitem.headline: Italian navy mounts rescue for Albanian boat.

text.p: A stricken boat packed with Albanians trying to flee to Italy was taken in tow by an Italian frigate on Wednesday when it ran into distress in rough seas in the Adriatic, the Italian Navy said.
A spokesman at Navy headquarters in Rome said the frigate Espero had attached a line to the vessel and was attempting to tow it slowly back into Albanian waters.
"It is a very delicate operation. They have to make sure the boat remains afloat," the spokesman said.

Several hundred people were on board, the spokesman said. Seven people, most of them children, had been winched off the boat by an Italian military helicopter before bad weather forced the aircraft to abandon further rescue attempts.

The Navy said the boat had run into trouble about 40 miles from the main Albanian port of Durres, a principal point of departure for more than 10,000 Albanians who have fled to Italy since March 13 after armed anarchy spread across the country.
They have crossed the Adriatic to southeastern Italian ports in a flotilla of rusting and ancient merchant and navy vessels, many of which Italian coastguards say are unseaworthy.
The spokesman said several Italian Navy ships and at least one U.S. Navy vessel were in the area of the rescue and were ready to join the operation if required.
